uncited: It sets itself apart from its parent [Hard and Soft Depth Regularization](9178-hard-and-soft-depth-regularization.md) by explicitly penalizing anisotropy (stretching) rather than just enforcing depth consistency, and from [Global-Local Depth Normalization](9179-global-local-depth-normalization.md) by operating on the scale parameters directly rather than depth values.
*   **Input:** The set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G}$, where each Gaussian $i$ has scaling parameters $\mathbf{s}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
Compute the L1 norm of the difference between the scale vector $\mathbf{s}_i$ and the mean scale vector $\tilde{\mathbf{s}}_i \cdot \mathbf{1}$.
Sum these differences over all Gaussians to obtain $E_{iso}$.
*   $\mathbf{s}_i$ is the scaling parameter vector for Gaussian $i$.
*   $\tilde{\mathbf{s}}_i$ is the mean of the components of $\mathbf{s}_i$.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of Gaussians $|\mathcal{G}|$, as it requires a single pass to compute mean scales and L1 norms.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Minimal, requiring only temporary storage for mean scales and differences.
